chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who killed another man accidentally during the sacred month. He said: 'The punishment is intensified upon him, and he must free a slave or fast for two consecutive months from the sacred months.' I said: 'Does this include something?' He said: 'What is it?' I said: 'The day of Eid and the days of Tashriq.' He said: 'He fasts, for it is an obligation that has become incumbent upon him.'

So it is not contradictory to what the first report contained regarding the prohibition of fasting on the two Eids, because the prohibition applies only to one who fasts them voluntarily and initially. But if two consecutive months become incumbent upon him according to what the report contained, then fasting these days becomes incumbent upon him because he included himself in that obligation.

As for fasting the days of Tashriq specifically, it has been narrated that the prohibition in them is restricted to one who is in Mina. But as for one who is in other towns, there is no harm in him fasting them.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th-13th of Dhul Hijjah)
key_terms.تَحْرِيمُ صِيَامِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ: Prohibition of fasting on the two Eids

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting during Eid and Tashriq days when performing the expiation for accidental killing?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) to resolve the apparent conflict between the prohibition of voluntary fasting on Eid and the obligation of fasting for kaffarah al-dam (expiation for accidental killing). The scholar clarifies that the prohibition is specific to those fasting voluntarily in Mina, whereas obligatory fasting for expiation takes precedence and applies universally, even during the days of Tashriq. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific obligations override general prohibitions in cases of necessity.
